title: GLES3: Fix index buffer target in mesh_surface_update_index_region
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

Closes [Trail3D (and mesh_surface_update_index_region) produce no geometry on Web: index buffer is bound to GL_ARRAY_BUFFER #124726](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/124726)

In `MeshStorage::mesh_surface_update_index_region()`, the index buffer was being bound to `GL_ARRAY_BUFFER` instead of `GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER`.

While desktop OpenGL drivers silently tolerate target mismatches for `glBufferSubData()`, OpenGL ES 3.0 and WebGL 2.0 strictly disallow binding a buffer allocated as `GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER` to a different target:
`WebGL: INVALID_OPERATION: bindBuffer: element array buffers can not be bound to a different target`

This caused dynamic index updates (such as those done each frame by `Trail3D` or procedural mesh updates) to fail on Web exports, causing the mesh to render no geometry.

## Additional information

The fix corrects the binding target in `mesh_surface_update_index_region()` to `GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER`.

In OpenGL ES / WebGL, the element array buffer binding is stored as part of the Vertex Array Object (VAO) state rather than global context state. We unbind the active VAO (`glBindVertexArray(0)`) before binding `GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER` so that unbinding the buffer at the end does not clear the element buffer of whatever VAO is currently active.

Additionally:
- Added a check to ensure `mesh->surfaces[p_surface]->index_buffer != 0` before updating to guard non-indexed surfaces safely.
- In `mesh_add_surface()`, marked `index_buffer` with `GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW` when `ARRAY_FLAG_USE_DYNAMIC_UPDATE` is specified (previously hardcoded to `GL_STATIC_DRAW`), matching how vertex, attribute, and skin buffers are handled.

## AI disclosure

AI was used to help research the WebGL specification constraints and analyze the VAO state binding behavior. I implemented the fix and verified the changes and formatting against the codebase.
